Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC Insolvency Disrupts Kyrgyz Mining Sector

Bishkek—Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC, a leading player in Kyrgyzstan’s metals and mining industry, has entered insolvency proceedings, causing immediate disruptions to its operations and raising concerns across the sector. The state-owned entity, known for its significant gold production, confirmed on Wednesday that a court-appointed administrator has taken control of day-to-day management.

Production at several mines has slowed sharply as suppliers halt deliveries pending clarification of outstanding payments. Employees at the company’s main processing facility in Jalal-Abad Province reported reduced shifts and uncertainty about future wages. “We have not received clear information about our jobs,” said Aibek Saparov, a site supervisor. “Everyone is anxious about what will happen next month.”

The Kyrgyz Metallurgical Workers’ Union estimates that more than 2,000 direct jobs are at immediate risk. “This is the largest disruption we have seen since independence,” stated union president Bakytbek Ismailov. “We urge the authorities to prioritize workers’ livelihoods and the stability of our national mining sector.”

Industry analysts say Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC’s insolvency exposes vulnerabilities in the country’s heavy reliance on commodities exports. “The impact on regional economies could be severe if operations are not stabilized quickly,” said Kamila Toktomatova, senior analyst at Bishkek Economic Research Institute.

The government has yet to announce a rescue plan, but officials have indicated that all options remain on the table. As the insolvency process unfolds, the sector faces continued uncertainty, with ripple effects expected to be felt across supply chains and regional budgets in the coming weeks.
